jobs.description:
Title:                                       Systems and Digital Solutions Intern

Type of contract:                   Paid internship

Contract duration:                 6 months   

Work time:                             Full-time (40 hours per week) or part-time

Reporting to:                         Systems and Digital Solutions Coordinator

Technical guidance:              BI and Systems Officer

Location:                                Remote (home-based outside Switzerland)

Start date:                              January 2027

Application deadline:           10/12/2026

 

Background

The Global Survivors Fund (GSF) was launched in October 2019 by Dr Denis Mukwege and Nadia Murad, 2018 Nobel Peace Prize laureates. Its mission is to enhance access to reparations for survivors of conflict-related sexual violence around the globe, thus responding to a gap long identified by survivors. GSF acts to provide interim reparative measures in situations where states or other parties are unable or unwilling to meet their responsibilities. GSF advocates for duty-bearers and the international community to develop reparations programmes. It also guides states and civil society by providing expertise and technical support for designing reparations programmes. GSF’s survivor-centric approach is the cornerstone of its work.

 

Role Summary

The Systems & Digital Solutions Intern provides part-time operational support across GSF’s systems, business intelligence, data quality, information management and IT support services. The intern contributes to first-line user assistance, routine administration, testing, documentation, data cleansing and validation, and the organisation of information within GSF Online, SharePoint and other approved systems. Assignments are prioritised through a six-month work plan and include a structured handover to support continuity between successive internship placements.

 

Position Responsibilities

Systems and User Support

  • Provide first-line support for GSF Online and other assigned systems, record support requests and contribute to an initial response within one business day;

  • Support routine user-account and access administration under supervision, including approved access requests and periodic access reviews;

  • Assist with system configuration, testing, issue reproduction and validation of fixes or new releases;

  • Escalate unresolved, recurring, security-related or access-control issues promptly.

Data Quality and Information Management

  • Support data cleansing, migration, validation and follow-up of identified data-quality issues;

  • Assist with routine data preparation and testing of Power BI dashboards and reporting outputs under technical guidance;

  • Support consistent organisation of information in SharePoint, GSF Online and other approved systems, including naming, storage and permissions;

  • Maintain clear records of completed checks, identified issues and follow-up actions.

Documentation, Training and Continuity

  • Prepare and update user guides, FAQs, process documentation and training materials;

  • Support system demonstrations, training sessions and user-adoption activities;

  • Complete priority assignments agreed through the six-month work plan and provide regular progress updates;

  • Prepare a structured handover of open tasks, documentation and learning for the next internship placement.

 

Position Requirements

Education and Experience

  • The position is open to students currently enrolled in a master’s program in information systems, data science, computer science, business analytics or a related field. Please note a tripartite agreement is mandatory for this internship;

  • Interest or initial experience in business systems, data quality, reporting, user support or information management;

  • Familiarity with Microsoft 365; experience with Power BI, SharePoint or similar platforms is an asset.

Other Requirements

  • Good written and spoken English; French or another GSF working language is an asset.

  • Analytical, organised and service-oriented approach, with attention to detail and confidentiality;

  • Ability to learn quickly, document work clearly and escalate issues appropriately;

  • Ability to work collaboratively in a multicultural and predominantly remote environment;

  • Commitment to GSF’s survivor-centred values, safeguarding, inclusion, accountability and responsible use of data and technology.

About the job

As a member of the AI model team, you will drive innovation in training and optimizing multimodal agents with a focus on real-world, interactive deployment. Your work will span the full agent development lifecycle - from data curation, interactive sandbox environments, and training pipeline design to model evaluation and optimization - with the goal of building multimodal agentic models that are both highly capable and practical to deploy locally at scale.

You will work across a wide spectrum of multimodal architectures integrating perception, reasoning, and tool execution across digital environments, applying state-of-the-art research to improve visual grounding, multi-step task completion, and adaptability to unseen interfaces. We expect you to bring a research-driven mindset combined with strong engineering discipline - someone who can identify the right technique for a given problem, implement it rigorously, and measure its impact clearly.

You will work closely with a small, high-caliber team where your contributions will have direct and meaningful impact. If you are passionate about pushing the boundaries of what multimodal agentic AI can achieve in production environments, this is your opportunity.

  • Conduct end-to-end research and engineering on multimodal agentic models capable of perceiving, reasoning, and acting across real-world digital environments - including desktop operating systems, web browsers, and mobile devices.

  • Architect high-concurrency interactive sandboxes (VMs, containers, and emulators) with fast snapshotting, deterministic resets, and reproducible evaluation frameworks to measure multi-step task completion and visual grounding.

  • Research and implement test-time adaptation and continual learning methods to enable rapid generalization to unseen applications and dynamic user interfaces.

  • Develop scalable multimodal agentic datasets, including synthetic trajectory generation, fine-grained UI grounding, and automated trajectory filtering and verification.

  • Drive model efficiency and local deployability on consumer hardware via knowledge distillation, quantization, and runtime optimization without degrading grounding or reasoning accuracy.

  • Translate frontier multimodal agentic research into production improvements, contribute to open-source ecosystems, and publish findings in top-tier AI conferences where applicable.

jobs.description:
Meet Siena

Siena is the Agent of Record for CX, built for consumer brands like Spanx, FIGS, Brooklinen, and Grüns.

It runs as a connected multi-agent stack on top of a shared intelligence layer: agents that sell, support, listen, handle social and voice across the entire customer journey, turning every conversation into signal you can act on.

The team

We are a small, fully distributed, global team. We have built leverage into how we work, which is what lets a team this size move at the speed we do.

We hire athletes. Everyone here owns real outcomes, defaults to writing over meetings, communicates with directness, and acts the moment they see something worth acting on. Low ego, high standards, fast clock.

If you want to set the bar rather than follow one, keep reading.

The Role

Siena's engineering team is small, senior and AI-native, and it ships across several products at once. This role leads a large part of that team, as a partner to engineering leadership, and owns how it scales. You will own delivery, hiring and team health for your part, and make sure a fast-moving team keeps shipping well across areas that look nothing alike. This is a hands-on leadership seat with a senior team and a lot of firefighting, not a layer of process.

What You'll Do

  • You will lead a large part of the engineering team, owning their delivery, priorities and growth.

  • You will own hiring and planning for your part of the team, and keep raising the bar.

  • You will turn shifting priorities into a plan the team can execute, and make trade-offs visible to leadership.

  • You will own problems wherever they land, switching from a security issue to a customer call to a technical design in the same day.

  • You will run on-call and incident response for your areas, and step in technically when the team needs it.

  • You will work with engineers and with teams across the company to find the better approach together, and make the call when one is needed.

Who You Are

The Bar: If you're missing any of these, this isn't the role for you.

  • You have managed software engineers directly.

  • You have owned hiring and planning for a team, and kept the bar high as the team grew.

  • You have taken over a team you did not build and made it better.

  • You have owned problems across unlike areas at once: technical, security and customer-facing.

Strong Signal: Not dealbreakers, but what separates a good hire from a great one.

  • You have low ego: you don't arrive with the answer, you work it out with the team, and you defend a view when it matters.

  • Your technical depth is still live: you can still ship code, drive an incident and use coding agents yourself.

  • You have made hard people calls (feedback, performance plans, promotions) and can walk through one.

  • You cut and rebalance scope as new needs come in, without losing the plot.

  • You have worked in an early-stage environment and delivered a result with little resource.

Nice to Have: Bonus, not required.

  • You bring a security-first approach to how a team builds and ships.

  • You are strong at prioritization: you rank competing requests and make the trade-offs clear.

  • You know the customer experience or e-commerce market.

  • You have shipped an AI agent product in production.

Not a Fit If:

  • You agree with whoever spoke last instead of bringing your own view.

  • You have not opened a pull request in years and see that as a strength.

  • You are looking for a large org to scale, or a domain specialist seat.

  • You want to set vision and direction rather than drive execution.

 

Why Siena?

Real ownership. You will own problems, not tasks, with the autonomy to solve them your way and the trust to do it without a manager in your inbox.

Work that ships and matters. What you build reaches real consumer brands fast.

A category we are creating. The Agent of Record is new ground, with unsolved problems and cutting-edge models, not a crowded field to compete in.

A team that respects your judgment. Globally distributed, async-first, low bureaucracy. We hire adults and treat you like one.

Great salary plus equity or stock grants. Own a piece of what you build.

Learning budget. If you are growing, so are we.

AI-fluency by default. Few places will push your work with production AI further or faster.

Our values

The people who thrive here are curious, customer-obsessed, and take ownership without being asked. They fix problems first and explain later. They're direct about feedback - both giving and receiving it - because they care more about getting things right than being polite.

They maintain high standards while moving at startup speed, and they build real relationships with teammates because they know that's how great work gets done. When things get tough, they adapt and keep pushing forward.

Our approach to AI

The people who thrive here treat AI like a natural extension of themselves. They've built their own ecosystem of agents - some for research, others for debugging, writing, analysis, or writing code. They know which AI works best for what problem.

Everyone gets premium accounts (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity Pro, Cursor, Lovable) plus a quarterly budget for new tools. But the magic happens in how we share knowledge. Demo days where someone shows off a clever workflows. Slack threads about which model handles a specific use case better. Learning from each other's AI workflows.

At Siena, we're not just looking for people who can do a job. We're looking for people who want to break boundaries, create the future, and reshape industries. If that's you, we look forward to your application.

How we hire

We use AI-assisted screening tools as part of our hiring process. All decisions are made by humans. You can request a human-only review at Siena provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.
